Subject: Follow-up from today — renewal scope & ops pain points

Thanks again for running through the numbers today, Marcus. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned heading into procurement: 

- Primary pain: RAG-related token surge during nightly ingestion + interactive queries is driving unpredictable spend spikes (we saw 3x on two days last month).
- SLA need: product team wants consistent p95 latency <= 350ms for UI calls (current p95 ~620ms at peak).
- Embeddings: cold-start for large batch embeddings (monthly jobs) plus a new search index pipeline due Q1. We need higher sustained throughput and lower unit cost for embeds.
- Reliability: want graceful degradation and a fallback model if peak capacity hits.

Can you send a short post-call recap with the proposed pilot scope (objectives + metrics), recommended infra (dedicated vs hosted), and an estimate for cost delta? Procurement also asked for an expected timeline to lock PO.

Appreciate it — Elena

--

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@conversations.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — renewal scope & ops pain points

Elena / Samir — thanks for the clear summary. Below is a concise post-call recap and recommended path. I attached a short pilot proposal and the usage snapshot we referenced.

Summary of pain points (confirmed)
- Cost volatility from RAG + ingestion windows (spike events causing 2–3x token cost on peak days).
- Unpredictable p95 latency for interactive queries (target <= 350ms).
- Embeddings throughput & cold-start for monthly index rebuilds.
- Need for an upgrade path that provides predictable unit economics and a fall-back for capacity issues.

Recommended immediate path (pilot) — 8 weeks
1) Dedicated reserved pool (initial 2x A100-equivalent units, autoscale policy with burst to shared capacity): reduces noisy-neighbor variability and provides baseline throughput.
2) KV/prefix caching for RAG hot prefixes + inference-side response caching for the UI path: expected token reduction on top-k hits.
3) Hybrid model profile for embeddings (quantized fp16/8 variant) to cut embedding unit cost ~25% while maintaining quality bucket.
4) Canary rollout + rollback policy for model variants; tracing hooks to validate quality against your seed prompts.

Pilot objectives & success metrics
- p95 latency for interactive path <= 350ms at 95% of production load tests.
- Reduce daily token spend volatility by 40% on peak days (measured vs baseline month).
- Achieve embedding throughput 5k/min for batch jobs within the dedicated pool and reduce embed cost/unit by ~25%.
- Demonstrate automatic fallback to hosted variant with <60s failover on saturation.

Timing & next steps
- Week 0–1: Kickoff & infra requirements (VPC peering/keys) — tech deep-dive with infra (Lauren to lead).
- Week 1–3: Provision dedicated pool, baseline tests, deploy caching hooks.
- Week 4–6: Controlled traffic canary, quality validation, cost telemetry.
- Week 7–8: Finalize runbook + SLA handover; prepare procurement packet.

Estimated commercial delta for pilot (ballpark)
- Incremental committed monthly (~$28k) for reserved capacity + burst budget; pilot credits can offset initial month. Exact numbers depend on selected instance types and region — I’ll follow up with a firm quote for procurement.

Attachments included:
- ConversationsAI_PilotProposal_v2.pdf (pilot scope + SOW)
- usage_report_oct2026.csv (30-day token/embeddings snapshot)

Action items:
- Lauren: can you confirm infra assumptions below (GPU type / NVMe caching availability)?
- Elena / Samir: share procurement timeline/PO target date (you mentioned mid-November).
- Marcus: follow up with a firm quote and a proposed kickoff slot next week.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
